proof:
# Whole residual bodies give disjoint unique-sector Minkowski credits

Let d>=2, m=d+1, and let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with their sole
dependence sum_i v_i=0. Let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies,
with (A+B)/2 contained in K, and B contained in the simplex

    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for every i}.

For every i define the actual endpoint unique-capture region and the
corresponding unique middle sector by

    R_i=A intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.x<-1},
    Z_i=K intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.x<0}.

Put r_i=|R_i|, b=|B|. For every index with r_i>0,

    (R_i+B)/2 subset Z_i,
    |Z_i| >= 2^(-d)(r_i^(1/d)+b^(1/d))^d.             (1)

The sectors Z_i are pairwise disjoint. Consequently, for EVERY set J
of positive-volume residual indices,

    |K intersect intersection_(l notin J){v_l.x<0}|
       >=2^(-d) sum_(i in J)(r_i^(1/d)+b^(1/d))^d.    (2)

If J is the full index set the left side means |K|. These are ordinary
d-volume statements about actual common bodies; no criticality or
global maximizing-source assumption is needed for them.

To prove the inclusion, take x in R_i and y in B. For j!=i,
v_j.(x+y)<-1+1=0. The midpoint lies in K by actual compatibility and
has all the required strict signs. The convex set R_i has positive
volume; its closure is a convex body and its boundary has zero volume.
Applying Brunn--Minkowski to that closure and B, or first to compact
inner convex exhaustions of R_i, proves (1). For explicit exhaustion,
choose p in int R_i and use p+(1-epsilon)(closure R_i-p), which is
contained in R_i for epsilon>0 and whose volume tends to r_i. Its
midpoint sum is contained in Z_i, so no boundary passage is needed on
the target set.

If x belonged to both Z_i and Z_j for distinct i,j, then all m values
v_l.x would be negative: the condition from Z_j supplies the missing
i-th inequality and conversely. Their sum would be negative, contrary
to sum v_l=0. Thus the Z_i are disjoint. Each Z_i with i in J satisfies
every inequality indexed outside J; adding their volumes proves (2).

In particular the original A captures U_j=|A intersect {v_j.x>=-1}|
give the actual lower bound

    r_i>=a-sum_(j!=i)U_j,       a=|A|,                (3)

by the union bound for their complements, with negative right sides
simply uninformative. This inequality does not replace the residual
regions by independent scalar variables.

For d=2, two present residuals R_i,R_j have a remaining index l. Their
disjoint middle sectors both miss the l-th middle cap. In an exact
three-fiber critical circuit with common cap mass Q and zero B captures,
the l-th middle cap has mass Q-U_l. Therefore (2) becomes

    k-Q+U_l >=
      [(sqrt(r_i)+sqrt(b))^2+(sqrt(r_j)+sqrt(b))^2]/4.  (4)

This retains the cross term sqrt(b)(sqrt(r_i)+sqrt(r_j))/2. It can be
compared with the separately proved swept-segment and injected-reserve
bounds, but cannot be added to those overlapping baselines without a
new disjointness proof. The quantitative one-thirty-second consequence
is proved in Section 8 of
`candidate 6b20e938071f0379`.
